subject: math.CA
name: Hilbert’s sixteenth problem for limit cycles
statement: For each fixed degree d, is there a finite bound H(d) on the number of isolated periodic orbits of every real planar polynomial vector field of degree at most d?
importance: It asks for a uniform understanding of oscillations in polynomial ordinary differential equations.
status_note: Finiteness for each individual polynomial vector field is known; a bound uniform over all coefficients, even at degree two, remains open.

subject: math.CA
name: Riemann hypothesis
statement: Does every nontrivial zero of the analytically continued Riemann zeta function have real part 1/2?
importance: It controls the sharp size of fluctuations in the distribution of prime numbers and the zeta function.
status_note: Many zeros and zero-free regions are known, but no proof covers every nontrivial zero.

subject: math.CA
name: Lindelöf hypothesis
statement: For every ε>0, is ζ(1/2+it) = O_ε((1+|t|)^ε) as |t|→∞?
importance: It predicts nearly minimal growth of the zeta function on its critical line and drives sharp analytic number-theory estimates.
status_note: The Riemann hypothesis would imply it; unconditional subconvex bounds still fall short of every positive exponent.

subject: math.CA
name: Irrationality of Euler’s constant
statement: Is the Euler–Mascheroni constant γ = lim_{n→∞}(Σ_{k=1}^n 1/k − log n) irrational?
importance: This fundamental constant occurs throughout asymptotic analysis, special functions, and probability.
status_note: Neither irrationality nor rationality has been proved; numerical digit computations do not decide either.

subject: math.CA
name: Irrationality of Catalan’s constant
statement: Is Catalan’s constant G = Σ_{n=0}∞ (−1)^n/(2n+1)² irrational?
importance: It is a central special value of the Dirichlet beta function and appears in classical integrals and lattice models.
status_note: Despite fast series and arithmetic estimates, irrationality of this particular beta value remains unproved.

subject: math.CA
name: Irrationality of ζ(5)
statement: Is the real number ζ(5) = Σ_{n=1}∞ n^(−5) irrational?
importance: It is a basic unresolved arithmetic property of an influential special-function value.
status_note: Apéry proved ζ(3) irrational, and infinitely many odd zeta values are irrational; those results do not identify ζ(5) individually.

references.title: Rivoal, La fonction zêta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs

subject: math.CA
name: Four exponentials conjecture
statement: If x₁,x₂ are complex numbers linearly independent over ℚ and y₁,y₂ are complex numbers linearly independent over ℚ, must at least one of exp(xᵢyⱼ), 1≤i,j≤2, be transcendental?
importance: It is a central proposed restriction on algebraic relations among complex exponential values.
status_note: The six exponentials theorem proves the analogous assertion for a 2-by-3 array; the 2-by-2 case remains open.

subject: math.CA
name: Erdős similarity conjecture
statement: For every infinite set A⊂ℝ, does there exist a Lebesgue-measurable set E⊂ℝ of positive measure containing no affine copy a+bA with b≠0?
importance: It asks which infinite patterns are forced inside arbitrary sets of positive measure.
status_note: Many patterns are known to be avoidable, but sufficiently fast-decaying sequences remain a major unresolved case.

references.title: Erdős similarity problem via bi-Lipschitz embedding

subject: math.CA
name: Mahler’s three-halves problem
statement: Does there exist a real ξ>0 such that the fractional part {ξ(3/2)^n} is less than 1/2 for every integer n≥0?
importance: This simple exponential-iteration question exposes deep limits of knowledge about fractional parts and multiplicative dynamics.
status_note: Such a ξ is called a Z-number. Neither existence nor nonexistence has been proved.

subject: math.CA
name: Sharp Beurling–Ahlfors norm conjecture
statement: For 1<p<∞, does the Beurling–Ahlfors singular integral on Lᵖ(ℂ) have operator norm p*−1, where p*=max(p,p/(p−1))?
importance: The sharp constant connects singular-integral analysis, quasiconformal mappings, and martingale inequalities.
status_note: The proposed value is a known lower bound and the p=2 case is proved; matching upper bounds for general p remain open.

references.title: Bañuelos and Janakiraman, Lp-bounds for the Beurling–Ahlfors transform
